name: Tapo P105

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). Bluetooth is used for setup only.

matter.note: TP-Link lists Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings for the P105, with no Matter. TP-Link sells separate Matter plugs with an M suffix (e.g. P100M).

apple_home.note: TP-Link's platform list for the P105 (Alexa, Google Assistant, SmartThings) leaves out HomeKit, and it has no Matter.

google_home.note: Link the Tapo account in the Google Home app or from the Tapo app.

alexa.note: Link the Tapo account through the Tapo skill.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings among the P105's platforms.

home_assistant.note: The official TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the P105. Tapo devices need your TP-Link account credentials to authenticate.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; TP-Link says no hub is required.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's integration talks to the plug on the local network. The Tapo app itself goes through the cloud.

energyMonitoring.note: TP-Link says the P110 and P115 measure energy; the P100 and P105 don't.

maxLoadWatts.note: 15 A, 1800 W at 120 V general use / resistive load; 1/6 HP motor.

summary: The Tapo P105 is a mini US Wi-Fi plug rated 15 A / 1800 W. It works with Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings through your Tapo account, with no hub, and Home Assistant's official TP-Link integration lists it. It has no Apple Home or Matter support and doesn't measure energy use.
caveats: No energy monitoring; the Tapo P115 is the mini plug with a power meter.
No Apple Home or Matter support.
Home Assistant needs your TP-Link account credentials to authenticate Tapo devices.
